pairs.question: Quare decimanus a decem potius quam a duobus, cum omnis ager eo fine in duas dividatur partes?
pairs.answer: Vt duopondium et duoviginti quod dicebant antiqui, nunc dicitur dipondium et viginti, sic etiam duodecimanus decimanus est factus.
pairs.derivation: Authorial rhetorical question and its own answer. The author asks why the limit is called decimanus (from 'ten') rather than from 'two' when the field is split into two parts, then answers with the etymological analogy: just as duopondium became dipondium, so duodecimanus became decimanus. Editorial angle brackets stripped keeping words (<di>pondium -> dipondium, eti<am> -> etiam, duo[de]cimanus -> duodecimanus); square-bracket-flagged words retained as they are the author's text. Answer ends at the full stop; the following sentence ('Kardo nominatur...') turns to a new topic.
